newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-MUSSINA AGREES TO THREE-YEAR EXTENSION WITH ORIOLES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-MUSSINA AGREES TO THREE-YEAR EXTENSION WITH ORIOLES.

text.p: Orioles ace Mike Mussina on Saturday agreed to terms on a three-year contract extension that will keep him in Baltimore through the 2000 season.
The right-hander, who is earning $6.825 million this year, will earn about $21 million over the three years of the new deal, according to Baltimore radio station WBAL.
"Mike is the foundation of our pitching staff and we are very pleased to have him signed through the millennium," said Orioles general manager Pat Gillick.
"He is one of the premier pitchers in the game and someone that we believe will be the anchor of our staff for the next several years."
A $7 million annual salary would place Mussina among the highest-paid pitchers in baseball.
Roger Clemens of Toronto earns the highest annual salary among pitchers after signing a three-year contract as a free agent in the off-season worth $24.75 million.
Cy Young Award winner John Smoltz of Atlanta is the highest-paid pitcher in the National League. He signed a four-year deal worth $31 million in November.

"I think the reason we wanted to do it was for that sense of security knowing where I was going to be next year and for the years after that," Mussina said after pitching in Saturday's 4-3 loss to Oakland. "I basically couldn't see myself playing anywhere else."
The 28-year-old Mussina owns the highest winning percentage (.689) among active major league pitchers with a 93-42 record.
He won 19 games in each of the last two seasons and has reached double figures in victories five times.
Mussina is 3-1 with a 3.99 ERA in six starts this season. He was 19-11 with a 4.81 ERA last season and established a club record with 204 strikeouts.
Mussina also became the first Orioles pitcher to win a Gold Glove award since Jim Palmer in 1979.
